newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul lifts local banks' overseas borrowing limits.
newsitem.headline: Seoul lifts local banks' overseas borrowing limits.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Friday it has repealed ceilings on local banks' overseas borowing.
The ministry said in a statement the move was aimed at improving local banks' international financing.
The ministry also lifted ceilings on equity-linked bond issues abroad by local companies, the statement said.

"It is necessary to strengthen the competitiveness of the financial industry as the nation steps up liberalisation after having joined the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (last year)," the statement said.
It said medium and long-term loans that South Korean banks borrowed overseas totalled $3.58 billion in 1996.
The restrictions on overseas borrowings had been introduced to maintain credit worthiness of local banks and to curb excessive inflows of foreign exchanges.
The ministry said overseas issues of equity-linked bonds, including convertible bonds and depositary receipts, amounted to $2.04 billion in 1996.
It said the liberalisation would help reduce financial costs for local banks and companies.
